title: Snake Through the Rows
statement:
You get the root of a binary tree. Return its values grouped by level, like a snake winding down the tree: row 0 (the root) is read left to right, row 1 right to left, row 2 left to right again, and so on, alternating.

Each row holds every node of that level, even when neighbours in the row have different parents. An empty tree gives an empty list.

Trees are written in level order with null for a missing child.

examples.why: Row 1 is read right to left, but row 2 must be back to plain left-to-right order. Flipping the order children are queued in, instead of flipping the row, gives [40, 51, 5, 18] there.
A row with one node reads the same both ways. Row 2 is a left-to-right row, so 8 comes first.

constraints: The tree is at most 500 levels deep
hints: Ignore the direction for a moment. How do you get the rows at all?
A breadth-first walk that handles one level per round gives each row left to right. The direction only changes how a finished row is written down.
Keep queuing children left then right as usual, and reverse every odd row before adding it (or write each value into its mirrored index). Do not change the queue order itself.

explain.intuition:
This is the plain row-by-row traversal with one twist on output. Collect each level left to right using a queue, processed one level per round. Then, for rows 1, 3, 5 and so on, reverse the row before storing it. The queue keeps its normal order, so the next level still comes out left to right.

The trap is trying to get the zigzag "for free" by changing the order in which children are queued. That reverses the order of parents for the next level as well as the order of siblings, and the effect compounds: by the third row the values come out in an order that is neither left-to-right nor right-to-left. If you want to avoid the reverse, write each value straight into its final slot: index i on even rows, size - 1 - i on odd rows.
steps: If the root is null, return []. Otherwise queue the root and set row = 0.
Each round, take size = queue length; that many nodes form the current level.
Dequeue them in order, collecting values left to right and queuing each node's left child, then its right child.
If row is odd, reverse the collected values. Append them and increase row.
Repeat until the queue is empty.
pitfalls: Swapping the order children are queued on odd rows. Row 1 looks right, row 2 comes out scrambled, as in the first example.
Starting with right to left. The root's row is left to right, so the first reversed row is row 1.
Flipping a global direction flag per node instead of per level. The direction belongs to the whole row.

solutions.title: BFS by level, reverse odd rows
solutions.idea: Collect each level left to right with a queue, and reverse the rows with an odd index before storing them.

solutions.title: Write each value into its mirrored slot
solutions.idea: Same level-by-level walk, but each value goes straight to index i or size - 1 - i, so no reverse is needed.

followups: Produce the snake order with two stacks instead of a queue. Which stack gets the left child first, and why?
Return the rows from the bottom level up, still alternating, with the bottom row read left to right.
